slot.brief: Three coplanar forces acting at a point; use equilibrium conditions to find the magnitude of one force.

stem: A ring is in equilibrium under three concurrent forces. Two forces are $8$ N east and $8$ N north; the third acts southwest. What is the magnitude of the third force?

verdicts.working: The first two forces have resultant magnitude \(\sqrt{8^2+8^2}=8\sqrt{2}\,\text{N}\) northeast. The southwest force must balance it, so its magnitude is \(8\sqrt{2}\,\text{N}\).

Independent check: The first two forces have resultant magnitude \(\sqrt{8^2+8^2}=8\sqrt{2}\,\text{N}\) northeast. The southwest force must balance it, so its magnitude is \(8\sqrt{2}\,\text{N}\).
solution:
For equilibrium, the southwest force must balance the resultant of the eastward and northward forces.
$$F=\sqrt{8^2+8^2}=8\sqrt{2}\,\text{N}$$
